# Compression and Quantization

Also called: 3DGS Compression, Gaussian Splatting Compression

## Overview
This family addresses the excessive memory footprint of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representations, which typically require hundreds of megabytes to gigabytes of storage for high-quality scenes [S1]. It solves this by reducing the precision of Gaussian attributes or restructuring the data layout to enable efficient entropy coding. Unlike [3D Gaussian Splatting Implementation Details](9128-3d-gaussian-splatting-implementation-details.md), which defines the raw representation, these methods optimize storage and transmission without altering the fundamental splatting rendering equation.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the pre-trained 3DGS parameters: positions $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^3$, scales $s \in \mathbb{R}^3$, rotations $q \in \mathbb{R}^4$ (quaternions), opacities $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, and spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients for view-dependent color. The core mechanism involves reducing the bit-depth of these attributes or reorganizing them into structures that exhibit spatial coherence, allowing standard compression codecs (e.g., JPEG XL, deflate, MPEG GPCC) to achieve high compression ratios. A common constraint is that position accuracy is critical for visual fidelity; thus, positions are often preserved at higher precision or handled separately from attribute quantization [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Codebook Quantization](23296-codebook-quantization.md)
A post-processing technique that replaces high-precision floating-point attributes with indices into a fixed-size codebook. It targets opacity, scale, rotation, and SH coefficients, preserving full precision for positions. It achieves ~27x memory reduction with minimal quality loss.

### [Improved RAHT-based Compression of 3D Gaussian Splats](23642-improved-raht-based-compression-of-3d-gaussian-splats.md)
Treats 3DGS as a point cloud with attributes, applying the Region-Adaptive Hierarchical Transform (RAHT) to decorrelate data. It applies transform coding to *all* attributes (including positions via voxelization) and requires no training pipeline changes.

### Gaussian Grid Layout
#### definition
- [S1] The process of converting a list of millions of 3D Gaussians into a 2D square grid structure to enable image-based compression.
#### step
- [S1] 1. Determine the largest square grid size (N x N) that can be completely filled with the current number of Gaussians. 2. Discard Gaussians with the lowest opacity values that do not fit into the grid.
#### pitfall
- [S1] Removing Gaussians with low opacity has minimal impact on visual quality (PSNR), whereas removing Gaussians with small scaling affects quality considerably more.
#### number
- [S1] On the Truck dataset, removing up to 30% of Gaussians (ordered by lowest opacity) does not meaningfully alter the scene's PSNR.
#### comparison
- [S1] Unlike standard 3DGS which stores Gaussians in an unordered list or .ply file, this method organizes them into a 2D grid to leverage spatial coherence for compression.

## Background
The original 3D Gaussian Splatting method [S1] demonstrated high-quality novel view synthesis but resulted in large file sizes (e.g., 615 MB for a single scene) due to the storage of millions of high-precision floating-point values. Subsequent research focused on compressing these representations for efficient storage and transmission, leading to methods like codebook quantization and transform-based compression.

## Sources
